not_covered: Based on the evidence provided, OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini in April 2025 to defend the reasoning-model frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push [Source: ev-1].
This launch signaled a direction for frontier capability as tool-using reasoning at commodity prices [Source: ev-1].

Regarding the specific details of this direction:
*   The models featured vision built directly into the model itself rather than being bolted on, along with native tool use (web search, code interpreter) trained into the model [Source: ev-1].
*   The release utilized an API-first strategy where developers had access from day one; specifically, o3 was not available in the ChatGPT app at launch, whereas o4-mini was [Source: ev-1].
*   OpenAI employed "budget forcing," which involves a fixed maximum thought budget with task-adaptive dynamic compute that allows harder questions to think longer [Source: ev-1].
OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled a direction for frontier reasoning models characterized by native integration of vision and tool use (web search, code interpreter) directly into the model architecture rather than bolting them on [Source: ev-1].
It also established an API-first availability strategy where developers had access from day one, with o3 initially excluded from the ChatGPT app while o4-mini was included [Source: ev-1].
The release highlighted OpenAI's adoption of "budget forcing," which uses task-adaptive dynamic compute to allow harder questions to think longer within a fixed maximum thought budget [Source: ev-1].
